the levels of TRab and TPO were significantly elevated in patients with Graves’ diseases (GD) as compared to SLES and normal subjects.

the levels of TRab and TPO in Omani patients were significantly higher than in SLE patients and normal subjects.

the determination of the level of TRAb and its relation to the level of TPO in patients with Graves’ diseases.
the determination of the levels of TRAbs with TPO in patients with Graves’ Disease.
the determination of the levels of anti-TRAb and TPO antibodies in Omani patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRAb and TPA are the most important autoantibodies in GD patients.
both TRAb and TPA are important in the pathogenesis and diagnosis of GD.
the results of this study show that the level of TRAb and thyroid peroxidases in Omani patients are significantly higher than those in the normal population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined that the levels of TRab and TPO in Omani patients are higher than those of normal healthy individuals and that the levels are higher in patients who have not been treated with iodine-131.
TRAb may be a good indicator for the diagnosis of GD and the efficacy of treatment in GD.
we have found high levels of TRAb as well as high levels of anti-Tyrosine Peroxidase antibodies (TgAb) in Omani Graves' Disease patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRAb may be useful in the diagnosis and treatment monitoring in Omani patients suffering from GD.
we have found a new marker of GD that may be helpful in diagnosis, monitoring of disease and treatment of GD.
